metadata.title: आदिवासी आस्था - सुरक्षा और प्रकृति संतुलन | Why do Indigenous People Apply White Clay On Body?
metadata.description:
This news explainer explores the deeper meaning behind the body markings of the Great Andamanese, Jarawa, Onge, and Sentinelese tribes. Far from decoration, these practices are closely linked to beliefs about health, protection, survival, and living in balance with nature.

Drawing on anthropological research, the video explains how white clay is used to cool the body and mask human scent, while red clay symbolises warmth, energy, and social identity. It reveals how these traditions function as a living survival system shaped by forest life and ancestral knowledge.

This story offers a rare insight into how indigenous cultures understand the relationship between the human body, nature, and the unseen world.
